title: Heavy rain and high winds on east coast threaten to disrupt Thanksgiving plans
summary:
Macy’s parade of balloons under threat in New York City as flights face delays or cancellations

Two storms that converged in the US south-east will move up the east coast, potentially…

blocks.text: Two storms that converged in the US south-east will move up the east coast, potentially disrupting plans for millions of Americans travelling to celebrate Thanksgiving with heavy rain, strong winds and possible flooding from Virginia to New York.
Strong winds expected to arrive in the north-east on Thursday could prevent the balloons from flying at the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York, where wind gusts could hit 60mph.
New York City’s emergency management commissioner, Christina Farrell, told WABC the city was considering starting the parade earlier than the scheduled 8.30am.

Farrell recalled that lightning and storms had come through the city on the Fourth of July. “It’s been that kind of year: the fireworks were moved up a little bit. That is one option. If the weather is coming in a little later, can we start things a little earlier?”
The balloon parade event, celebrating its 100th anniversary this year, has only been grounded once before, when weather kept them deflated in 1971.

New York City guidelines say that the inflatables cannot fly if sustained winds exceed 23mph or if wind gusts surpass 34mph. (These guidelines were introduced after wind gusts of up to 40mph blew a “Cat in the Hat” balloon into a lamp-post in 1997 and falling debris injured a spectator.)

The storm is forecast to move over Cleveland, Buffalo and New England later on Thursday, with up to five inches of rain, and wintry weather could appear in the Mississippi valley and upstate New York.

The National Weather Service said “powerful wind gusts of 50 plus mph are forecast along the coast, with 45 plus mph gusts inland to the I-95 corridor and central Appalachians. Power outages and tree damage are possible.”
It added: “Coastal residents and those traveling on the East Coast over Thanksgiving are urged to prepare for coastal flooding, strong winds, and possible power outages.”

AccuWeather’s vice-president of forecast operations, Dan DePodwin, said the “potent storm comes at a time when millions of people are traveling and businesses are preparing for the holiday season. A significant deterioration in the weather is expected to spread northward along and east of the Appalachians Wednesday through Friday.”

Flights to or from Miami, Orlando, Raleigh-Durham, Charlotte and Atlanta on Wednesday are expected to face delays. FlightAware showed 738 delays within, into, or out of the United States today and 30 cancellations.

Residents of south Florida could see up to 8 inches of rain, damaging wind gusts and brief tornadoes on Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service Miami. The service said flooding was a concern across east-central Florida, especially the Treasure Coast, Brevard and Okeechobee counties.
Recent communications-related outages at the nation’s airports have put air travel in the crosshairs of public dissatisfaction.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that passengers on domestic flights were being trapped between the gate and the runway for more than three hours at rates not seen in more than 15 years, it said.

On the Pacific coast, high tides associated with the “Beaver” supermoon could break 40-year-old records and flood low-lying coastal communities, with tides peaking on Wednesday at 2.8ft above normal in the San Francisco Bay Area, according to Dial Hoang, a National Weather Service forecaster.
